messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: apac1c ingress cluster experiencing 502/conn-reset spike. Alerting SRE oncall.

alice: Acked. I’m on it — will gather metrics and check ALB/Envoy.

sam: I’m pulling logs now. Initial glance: envoys in apac1c show repeated `RST` from upstream, TLS handshakes ok, then immediate reset. Example from envoy logs: ```[2026-03-15T03:12:05Z] cluster_outbound_8080 reset connection: ECONNRESET (peer=10.0.12.7:52000)```

maria: ALB target group shows unhealthy hosts too. Health checks failing ~3x for several instances. Health check path `/healthz` returning 502 on failing hosts.

alice: 5xx rate for apac1c ingress cluster = 18% over last 5m (normal <0.5%). P50 latency up 2x. Dashboard: https://console.internal/redwood/metrics?cluster=apac1c (linked)

sam: Running `kubectl -n ingress get pods -o wide` — pod restarts are low, but node network error logs show `rx ring reset` flapping on ena driver. This looks like NIC-level flakes.

maria: We pushed a host kernel/driver update in apac1c last night as part of unattended maintenance window. Ops notes: AMI roll started 02:00 UTC. Could be related.

alice: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Drain affected nodes / respin instances (roll ASG). 2) Shift traffic away from apac1c to other regions via Route53 weighted change. 3) Increase retries/fallback at proxy layer.

eng-oncall: Draining will help but will take ~10-15 minutes per node and could reduce capacity. If driver is causing packet drops, respins likely help.

product-ops: Any customer-visible impact? We already have inbound support tickets for chat timeouts (CS-4521). Need ETA to share with affected customers.

alice: Quick customer impact summary: - ~35% of requests hitting apac1c experiencing errors/timeouts (global % lower) - A small set of customers (APAC-heavy) reporting increased errors - No data corruption, only request failures. Creating incident INC-2026-345.

sam: Trying a small test: curl to one failing pod ip: `curl -v http://10.0.12.7:8080/healthz` -> returns 502. Re-run `tcpdump` shows NIC queue resets.

maria: Recommendation: perform region-weighted DNS shift to reduce APAC traffic by 80% to eu-west-1 while we roll nodes. Route53 change with low TTL (if set) will take effect within TTL; current TTL was 60s, good.

alice: I can execute the Route53 weight change. Plan: update RR set to send 80% weight to eu-west-1 ALB, 20% remain in apac1c. Then roll nodes (ASG replace) and monitor.

ryan: I’ll take the oncall handoff in 20m. If you need immediate reboot/replace I can execute.

sam: Patch rollout plan for apac1c nodes: - Mark node unschedulable, drain ingress pods - terminate instance (ASG will replace with latest AMI without the faulty kernel) - wait for healthcheck green - continue to next node. Run parallel on max 2 nodes at a time.

alice: Executing Route53 change now. Command: ```aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z1EXAMPLE --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.example.","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-west-1","Weight":80,"AliasTarget":{"HostedZoneId":"Z2EWEST","DNSName":"alb-eu-west-1.example."}},{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.example.","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"apac1c","Weight":20,"AliasTarget":{"HostedZoneId":"Z3APAC","DNSName":"alb-apac1c.example."}}}]}'```

incident-bot: Change submitted (ChangeId: C123456789). Route53 propagation should start immediately given 60s TTL.

support-bot: Noted: I’ve posted a short customer message to the incident status page: "APAC region experiencing ingress errors; mitigation in progress. We are shifting traffic and rotating hosts."

sam: Starting node rotations on apac1c now — replacing 2 nodes in parallel (node-42, node-43). Logs show node-42 terminated, replacement booting.

maria: After replacing node-42, ALB health checks for that target group are green. Envoy resets reduced on new instance.

alice: Metrics update: apac1c 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 6% within 8 minutes of weight change + first replacements. Global error rate down ~4%.

ryan: Taking oncall handover. Alice, handing off console access and Route53 permissions. I’ll continue rotations and monitor customer impact. :white_check_mark:

alice: Handing off. Steps completed: Route53 change (80/20), started ASG replacements, posted customer note. Next steps: finish rolling rest of nodes, keep weight at 80/20 until all nodes healthy for 30m, then gradually return weight back.

product-ops: Thanks team. We’ll update customers with a 30m ETA.

sam: After full roll (4/6 nodes replaced so far) 5xx for apac1c at 1.2% — near baseline. Will finish remaining nodes in next 20m.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-345 assigned to oncall ryan. Severity: Sev2.

ryan: Closing loop — once rotations complete and 30m steady-state, I’ll revert Route53 weight to pre-incident config and post a resolved note.

alice: Nice job. Marking mitigation successful so far. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Customer update posted: "Mitigation in progress; traffic temporarily shifted; rolling host replacements under way. We will update in 30 minutes."

maria: Root cause hypothesis: kernel/ENA driver combination from last-night AMI roll causing NIC ring resets under production load. Action: block that AMI, revert auto-roll, and run broader canary before next wave.

alice: Action items: [1] Block faulty AMI in builder; [2] Add pre-roll NIC stress smoke test to AMI pipeline; [3] Post-mortem after incident is stabilized.

ryan: I’ll update INC-2026-345 with notes and run post-mortem template tomorrow.

support-bot: Update posted to customers at 03:56 UTC.

alice: Last check-in: all nodes rotated, apac1c 5xx = 0.6% over last 10m. Reverting Route53 weight to baseline in 5m if stable.

sam: Reverting weights now. Command similar to above to set original weights.

incident-bot: Route53 change submitted (ChangeId: C123456790).

alice: Closing incident after monitoring window. Will schedule post-mortem next business day. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
